The function $f(x)$ is represented by the mapping diagram above. What is ${f}^{-1}(4)?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The function ${f}^{-1}(x)$ reverses the action of $f(x),$ as depicted below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14208916/assets/a0194a90466532c723c904d5ef9fea394e976b8b1f5287f066d5843f575e762e.png)

 

From the above, we see that ${f}^{-1}(4)=5.$

**Method 2**

From the given mapping diagram, we have:

$$
f(5)=4
$$

Applying ${f}^{-1}$ to both sides of the above equation, and using the fact that ${f}^{-1}(f(x))=x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(f(5)) & ={f}^{-1}(4) \\ 5 & ={f}^{-1}(4)\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that ${f}^{-1}(4)=5.$
